belief: I have to earn my place in any group.
origins: Where acceptance was handed out for performance, such as grades, athletics, usefulness, or obedience, we learn that belonging is a wage. In new groups, we over-work, over-give, and fear being found out as ordinary. We may not know how to simply be a member.
teaches: Paul writes, “Accept one another, then, just as Christ accepted you, in order to bring glory to God.” “For it is by grace you have been saved through faith, and this not from yourselves; it is the gift of God, not by works.” John says, “to all who did receive Him… He gave the right to become children of God.” Scripture also says, “The LORD your God is among you… He will rejoice over you with gladness.” In God’s family, a place is given, not earned. Healthy communities reflect this, and we can look for those that do.
self_statements: I have to prove myself first.
I have to be useful to be kept.
They will accept me only if I perform.
If I stop earning it, I will be out.
I owe the group before I get a place.
errors: Insisting that I must earn acceptance.
Predicting removal if I stop performing.
Believing I am either contributing or expendable.
Feeling anxious and concluding that my place is at risk.
questions: Where did I learn that a place has to be earned?
Have I seen people who were simply welcomed? What was that like?
What do I do in groups out of fear?
What does God say about my place in His family?
What would it feel like to just show up?
Which group treats people as welcome without conditions?
truth: In God’s family, my place is a gift. I can contribute out of joy, not fear, and look for groups that accept people as they are. I do not have to earn a seat at God’s table.
hw_truths: Grace is a gift, not a wage.
I have the right to be a child of God.
I can contribute out of joy.
log: Each week, note one moment you were accepted without performing.
actions: Write what you do to earn a place.
Accept an invitation or kindness without repaying.
prayer: Father, Christ accepted me. Free me from earning my place. Help me contribute out of joy and look for communities that welcome people as they are. Amen.
hw_questions: What do I do out of fear?
What if I just showed up?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Christ accepted me, so my place is a gift.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “I have to earn my place in any group.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
